findings.title: Loose any-match validation of array-valued iss/sub/nonce/jti claims bypasses claim pinning
findings.evidence: validateClaimValues now matches with `if (!values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v))))` (line 159). Upstream fast-jwt 5.0.6 has two distinct matchers: an `.every(...)` scalar matcher and a `.some(...)` validateClaimArrayValues used ONLY when the validator sets `array: true` (aud). This copy deleted validateClaimArrayValues and the `else if (array)` routing branch in verifyToken (lines 223-227), so the `.some` matcher is now applied to EVERY string claim, including iss/sub/nonce/jti which are registered without array:true (lines 466-484). validateClaimType (lines 144-152) only checks that element types equal 'string'; it never enforces that a non-array claim is a scalar, so a token whose iss is an array passes the type check and then only needs ONE element to equal the configured allowedIss. Reachability: verifyToken loops validators (line 209), normalizes payload[claim] into `values` (lines 210-212), type-checks it, then calls validateClaimValues at line 226 which reaches the loose `.some` at line 159. Runtime PoC with secret 'topsecret' and allowedIss 'https://trusted.example': this copy ACCEPTS iss=["https://evil.example","https://trusted.example"], while upstream 5.0.6 rejects it with FAST_JWT_INVALID_CLAIM_VALUE (scalar iss='https://evil.example' is rejected by both). Precondition: the attacker must present a token that is validly signed by the trusted key but whose iss/sub/nonce/jti is an array containing the trusted value (e.g. a shared/multi-tenant signing key or an issuer that emits array claims); under that precondition the verifier treats the token as issuer/subject/nonce-valid while carrying extra attacker-chosen values that downstream code reading payload.iss/payload.sub will trust, defeating issuer/subject pinning and the intent of allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedNonce.
